title: Policy Regret for Wasserstein-Barycenter Welfare with Nested Measure-Valued Outcomes
banked_reason: Cold D0.5 rated the mathematically valid, noncolliding matched n,m,d frontier at subfield: projected paper-score ceiling 7.3 falls below the field threshold 7.4, with no in-scope improvement directive.
gap_reasons: Its significance remains concentrated in one lower-half utility, equal randomization, finite-cell policies, and conditionally independent readings; it does not deliver a broadly applicable distributional policy-learning framework.

No numerical implementation or finite-sample study establishes the usefulness of the conservative polynomial tuning for trial planning, and the CGM example supplies neither utility validation nor independent-reading validation.
paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a matched rate-order minimax frontier for the lower-half barycenter utility over an atom-allowing quantile-Lipschitz class, with an explicit finite-reading rule and legal all-rule lower witnesses. A D0 persistence failure was recovered from saved solver output, all five cited leaves were source-attested, and only the critical-constant question remains open. Cold D0.5 review found no theorem collision but capped the delivered package at subfield; inert graph and related-work cleanup was left as recorded review debt because it could not raise the field score.
tldr: In an iid randomized study with two treatments and \(d\) covariate cells, each participant supplies \(m\) conditionally independent readings from the assigned outcome measure. Potential measures have support \([0,1]\) and nondecreasing \(U\)-Lipschitz quantiles for fixed \(U>0\); atoms are allowed. For lower-half Wasserstein-barycenter welfare, the all-rule minimax expected regret is \(\asymp_U\min\{1,\sqrt{d/n}+[m\min\{m,\log(e+n/d)\}]^{-1}\}\), attained by the explicit data-only global-local factorial-score rule without a minimum cell mass. Absolutely continuous lower witnesses give the converse by inclusion. Matching the full-measure order requires \(m\min\{m,\log(e+n/d)\}\gtrsim_U\sqrt{n/d}\) as \(n/d\to\infty\). The completed theorem-level audit identifies no generic theorem that evaluates this fixed-functional binomial channel and yields the matched all-rule \(n,m,d\) causal policy-regret frontier. Exact critical constants and constant optimality remain open.
gap: Published work separately covers fully observed Wasserstein policy learning, fixed-barycenter nested sampling, general functional duality, broader-class bounded-reading nonidentification, and whole binomial-mixing-law recovery. None evaluates the integrated common-random-measure score and legal causal-policy converse needed for the joint \(n,m,d\) frontier.
fill: An endpoint-corrected global-local factorial score and scaled adjacent-interval moment-matched subexperiment deliver matching all-rule regret bounds, sparse-cell validity, bounded-depth ambiguity, and the full-measure equivalence threshold.
